finish._cont_route_planes_why: 12 September 2026: the continuation exports its own DSN, and it did so with every plane REMOVED, because finish.sh passed it no plane treatment and routeflow never put one in the finish's environment either. It is the same treatment the route itself is given in routeflow/<phase>.json, and a test holds the two in agreement.

finish._direct_close_why: 12 September 2026, A24. Declared for A alone: C10's eleven opens are 39 to 298 mm and this tool declines every one of them, which is the correct answer and not a reason to run it there. The re-finish of A35 spent all 1,800 seconds on FIVE of thirteen open pairs and stopped in the middle of a shape, reporting 'the budget ran out' for the eight it never reached. Each candidate costs a design-rule check and this board's DRC is seven seconds (240 by 160 mm, six layers, 5,000 tracks), so thirteen pairs at roughly ten shapes each is an hour of DRC before anything else. Ninety minutes is that with room; it is wall time on a box that is at four percent of its cores, and the alternative is a stage that reports a budget rather than an answer. It lives INSIDE this block because finish.sh's cfg strips a `direct_close_` prefix and looks in here: declared at the finish level it was read as a key of a block that does not have it, and the stage spent 1,809 seconds of an 1,800 second default while the declaration said 5,400. _gnd_grid_why: MEASURED ON THIS BOARD, 17 September 2026, and NOT declared. A41 declares gnd_grid 2.1 mm and A40 does not; same tree, same tools, same board, same router invocation and the same five hour cap. The grid lays 4,000 locked ground vias (the routed board carries 4,650 vias against A40's 902). Rule RET-004, each board judged at its own stem beside its own intent so the classification is the rule's: A41 reads 33 signal vias without a ground via within 1.5 mm of 52 judged, A40 reads 46 of 58. So the grid answers thirteen of them and leaves thirty-three; it does not close the rule. It costs this board nothing in copper terms that showed: 23 open connections against 25 at the cap, and pour_stitch found 0 islands to repair against 4. That is the opposite of board C, where the grid cost 21 open connections, and of board P, where it cost the route. WHY IT IS STILL NOT DECLARED: the board this tree holds is A32, which is 0 hard and 0 unrouted and reads 32 lacking of 40 judged, while BOTH arms are open boards that their own finishes refused. A grid that does not close the rule is a change to make when the rule's criterion is ruled (owner decisions 32 and 39), not before, and 4,000 extra drilled vias on a six-layer board is a fabrication cost to put to the owner with that ruling rather than to take quietly.
_annular_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, annular ring rows, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): six layers at 1 oz outer: multilayer 1 oz, recommended 0.20 mm or above. The RECOMMENDED figure is taken and not the absolute minimum, because the absolute minimum is where yield starts to suffer and this board is made five at a time with no second chance before the owner has it in his hands.
_stitch_cap_mm_why: Rule RET-003, 16 September 2026. Board A's In2 carries a GND pour and a VBAT pour side by side, and 35 of its signal vias change reference between the two: measured with ref_change.py, which samples the fill in a ring around each via because the fill retreats from the via's own barrel. A return current that has to cross between two different reference conductors crosses at a capacitor or it goes the long way round, so the question is how far that capacitor may sit. THREE MILLIMETRES IS OURS, not a source: it is the same distance this project already declares for a decoupling capacitor from the pin it serves, and using one number for the same physics is better than using two. The rule stays GENERATED_ONLY until a document states it.
_via_ring_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002, the VIA rows rather than the annular ring row. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): minimum via diameter 0.25 mm on a minimum via hole of 0.15 mm for 2 or more layers, which leaves 0.05 mm of copper per side. The PTH annular ring row (0.20 mm) is stated for a plated COMPONENT hole and cannot bind a via, because no via at this document's own minimum could satisfy it; board D12 was refused on 16 September for a 0.45/0.20 via at 0.125 mm of ring, which is what that confusion costs.

_external_ports_why: Rule TRN-001, 16 September 2026. A port that leaves the ENCLOSURE is a wire a person will plug something into, in the rain, having walked across a floor. Every one of them reaches a semiconductor, and the only thing between is a suppressor, a choke, a series resistor into a clamp, or nothing. Most connectors on these boards are internal (board-to-board ribbons, module sockets, fan leads inside a sealed case) and treating every J as external would refuse every board for wires that never leave it. The board knows which is which and nothing else does, so each one is named with where it goes.

_prelay_nets_why: MEASURED AND REFUSED, 17 September 2026. A40 pre-lays /CH_ACN, /CH_SRP, /FE_LDRV1 and /PD_EN on all four copper layers before the router sees the board; A42 is A40 with that stage removed and nothing else changed (its chain log carries guard-prelay-group and no guard-prelay). _sense_clearance_why: WHY THE TWO SENSE LINES RUN TOO CLOSE, and what the fix has to reckon with (17 September 2026, rule ANA-001). POE_CS runs 0.182 mm from POE_SW2 over 10.79 mm and B33_FB 0.350 mm from B33_SW over 8.47 mm, both outside the shared part's courtyard, and the declaration asks 0.50 mm. THE ROUTER DID WHAT THE CLASSES TOLD IT: POE_CS is in class SW at 0.127 mm of clearance and POE_SW2 in HV at 0.18, so 0.18 is the bar it honoured, and B33_FB is in no pattern at all and falls to Default. The obvious fix is a SENSE class at the 0.50 mm the declaration asks for, which the router would honour because a class reaches the DSN; what it has to reckon with is that a class clearance has no courtyard exemption, so 0.50 mm would also apply where the sense line approaches the shunt's own pads, which is where it must go. Measure that geometry on the board before declaring the class: if the shunt's pad gap cannot hold 0.50, the class is the wrong instrument and the answer is placement. Freerouting reads DSN classes and not KiCad's custom rules, so a per-net-pair keep-away cannot be expressed any other way. MEASURED, AND THE CLASS IS REFUSED (17 September 2026, same hour). Pad edge to pad edge on A42's board, the nearest OTHER-NET pad to each conductor's own pads: POE_CS is 0.820 mm from the FETs' own switching pads at Q18 and Q19, 0.660 from their gate drives, 1.760 at the divider R72, and **0.250 mm at U16 pin 16**, the controller's own fine-pitch pin, whose neighbour is GND; B33_FB is 0.850 mm at both divider resistors and **0.200 mm at U12 pin 8**, whose neighbour is B33_SS. A 0.50 mm class has no courtyard exemption, so it would refuse the escape at those two pins and the route would die at the source rather than ten millimetres away. So the class is the wrong instrument at 0.50: what is left is a smaller class value that the pins can hold (0.25 is the floor those two pins set), or PLACEMENT, putting the sense network so its run stays inside the courtyard the rule already exempts, or a declared exemption per net with its reason. The placement is the one that answers the rule as written.

_rf_line_why: ELEVEN RF PORTS AT 26 OHM, AND THE WIDTH IS NOT WHAT IS WRONG (17 September 2026, rule RF-001, which this board was outside of until its board list was corrected to match its own condition). Every one of board A's eleven RF nets runs EXACTLY 10.0 mm on In2.Cu at 0.35 mm, which the board's own stackup makes a 26 ohm stripline against the class's 50 ohm target, 49 percent low. The width is right: board D carries the same 0.35 mm RF class and passes RF-001 on twelve segments, because its runs are on an OUTER layer, where 0.35 mm is about 50 ohm. What board A has is a LAYER problem, and it comes from the geometry: J_RF<k> is the SMA jack on the top and J_BM<k> the SMP-MAX blind-mate receptacle on the UNDERSIDE, 10 mm south of it, so every port has to cross the board and the router took the whole crossing on one inner layer rather than a short run and a transition. The eleven lengths being identical to a tenth of a millimetre is what says it is systematic. THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, for the generation after A43: lay each port yourself, locked, as an outer-layer run from the jack to a point over the receptacle with a single via into its pad, which is the geometry board D already passes on; the cost has to be measured first, and this board's own arms say pre-laid copper is EXPENSIVE on it, the other way round from the first reading of this note: the routeflow journals have A40, which pre-lays four nets, at 25 unrouted of 254 and A42, which is A40 with those four removed and nothing else changed, at 15, so pre-laying cost this board ten connections and half again the time per pass. A43 routes without them. What is different about the eleven RF drops is that each is 10 mm in the south edge between two FIXED parts rather than a crossing of the board, and that they are already laid, by the router, on the wrong layer: the choice is not whether that copper exists but who chooses its layer. Nothing was changed while A43 routes. CORRECTED AND ANSWERED THE SAME EVENING (appendix 32.221): the width IS part of what is wrong, because board D passes at 0.35 mm on an outer layer for its 7628 four-layer stack's 0.2 mm of prepreg under F.Cu, and this six-layer 3313 stack puts 0.0994 mm (er 4.1) there: rf_line's own microstrip form with its 0.967 correction reads 0.35 mm on this board's F.Cu as 22.8 ohm, 0.15 as 48.2 and 0.14 as 50.1. gen_pcb_a3.py lays the eleven drops itself now, locked on F.Cu from the SMA centre pin to the blind-mate centre pin, straight and clear of every other net's copper on the placement, and the RF class is 0.14 mm; the first regeneration at 0.35 mm read all eleven at 23.5 ohm and the board's placed gate, escapes and hard set were unchanged (0 hard).
